CHARACTER LIBRARY

Saved and imported characters appear here, ready for any episode.

Import rules & free characters
  • Format: .glb (glTF 2.0 binary) or .vrm, up to 40 MB, under 300k triangles (120k or fewer renders fastest).
  • Skeleton: a humanoid rig with hips, spine, neck, head, both arms and hands (legs recommended). Mixamo, VRoid/VRM, Rigify and Character Creator names are recognised.
  • Lip sync: mouth shapes named as Oculus visemes (viseme_aa…), ARKit (jawOpen, mouthSmile…), VRoid (Fcl_MTH_A…) or VRM expressions; otherwise a jaw bone.
  • Blink & feelings: eyeBlink / Fcl_EYE_Close / VRM blink, and happy/angry/sad/surprised shapes are used when present.
  • Not supported: Draco or Basis/KTX2 compressed files. Re-export without compression.
  • Free sources: VRoid Studio (make anime characters, export .vrm), Mixamo (free auto-rig and characters, download FBX then convert to .glb in Blender), Blender (File → Export → glTF 2.0). Use characters you have the rights to.

The stage turns to show this character while you edit. Open the Scene tab to return to the story camera.

WORLD & BACKGROUND
ANIMATED EFFECTS
World rules & free sources
  • 360° background: an equirectangular image (twice as wide as tall), .hdr, .jpg or .png, up to 60 MB; 4096 px wide or more looks best. Characters stand on its ground and are lit by it.
  • 3D world: a .glb scene up to 80 MB and 2 million triangles; Draco, KTX2 and meshopt compression are fine. Its animations loop on the film clock. Leave an open area about 10 m across at the centre for the cast, or use Move/Turn/Scale to place it.
  • Free sources: Poly Haven (CC0 HDRIs and models), Kenney and Quaternius (CC0 low-poly worlds and animated animals), Sketchfab (check each model's licence). With BlenderMCP, Claude can build a scene in Blender for you to export as .glb.

THE SCRIPT

Write the whole episode.

One line per spoken line. Tags in brackets set the feeling, action and camera. A >> SCREEN line changes the monitor on the next line.

FormatREN [worried, facepalm]: Line here.MICA [idea, raise, pause=0.8]: Line.>> SCREEN alert: KICKER | Title | Subtitle>> SCREEN info +progress: … | … | …FeelingsActionsCamerasKAI [cu:mica]: frames MicaKAI [cam=90/15/3.5/50, move=orbit]: 360° angle

Paste the prompt into Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini (free plans work), then paste the script it writes back here.
